chunks: Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Fitrah (poor tax), who are its people, those upon whom it is obligatory? He said: 'Whoever finds nothing.'

key_terms.أَهْلُهَا: The people entitled to receive it
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah, a specific alms tax given to the poor during Ramadan
key_terms.مَنْ لَا يَجِدُ شَيْئًا: One who finds nothing (i.e., has no wealth or means)

ai.seo_question: Who is eligible to receive Fitrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the threshold for Fitrah recipients as those who possess no assets whatsoever ('man la yajid shay'an'), a criterion that Shia jurists distinguish from the broader poverty definitions used for Zakat. This strict definition underscores the specific charitable obligation of Fitrah, ensuring it reaches the most destitute members of the community during Ramadan, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise legal boundaries in almsgiving.
